I've been working this land for 40 years. I know Quzhou's soil — sandy loam on the North China Plain, prone to drought, and my well gives me control others don't have. My household is just two of us now, and my son sends money back from the city, so I'm not desperate for cash. But I still run this farm properly.

My wheat-maize rotation is the backbone. Those 10 mu cycle together every year — winter wheat goes in October, comes out in June, then summer maize fills the same ground through September. That's efficient, it's what the land is suited for, and I can manage it mostly alone with machinery hire. I keep 5 mu in cotton for the cash premium, though picking is hard with just two of us. I won't expand cotton — the labor isn't there.

For wheat, I'll use an improved variety like Jimai 22. I apply base fertilizer before sowing and top-dress at jointing. Three irrigations: pre-winter sealing water, jointing stage, and heading. Rotary tillage keeps things manageable after decades of this system.

For maize, I go straight hybrid — Zhengdan 958 or similar. I direct-seed into the wheat stubble, no tillage needed. Fertilizer is heavier on nitrogen since maize is a hungry crop. Two irrigations at jointing and tasseling unless we get rain.

For cotton, I deep plough — cotton roots need depth, and I rotate it off the grain plots. Hybrid Bt cotton reduces some pesticide burden but I still spray for aphids and bollworm. Four irrigations, heavier K to support boll development.
